enonce.texte:
Read each sentence and identify which conditional form is being used: Zero Conditional, First Conditional, Second Conditional, or Third Conditional.

  1. If you heat water to 100°C, it boils.
  2. If I study hard, I will pass the exam.
  3. If I had more money, I would travel the world.
  4. If she had arrived on time, she wouldn't have missed the meeting.
  5. If it rains, the ground gets wet.
  6. If we leave now, we will catch the bus.
  7. If I were you, I would accept the offer.
  8. If he had studied, he would have passed.

questions.texte: Identify the type of conditional in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. Zero, 2. First, 3. Second, 4. Third, 5. Zero, 6. First, 7. Second, 8. Third

sousQuestions.texte: What is the structure of the Third Conditional?
sousQuestions.reponse: If + past perfect, would have + past participle

enonce.texte:
Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in parentheses. Use Zero or First conditional.

  1. If you _______ (mix) red and blue, you _______ (get) purple.
  2. If she _______ (study), she _______ (pass) the test.
  3. If I _______ (have) time, I _______ (help) you.
  4. If you _______ (not water) plants, they _______ (die).
  5. If he _______ (call), I _______ (tell) him the news.

questions.texte: Complete the sentences with the correct verb forms.
questions.reponse: 1. mix, get; 2. studies, will pass; 3. have, will help; 4. don't water, die; 5. calls, will tell

sousQuestions.texte: Explain the difference between Zero and First conditional.
sousQuestions.reponse: Zero conditional is for general truths (if + present, present). First conditional is for real future possibilities (if + present, will + infinitive).

enonce.texte:
Transform the following sentences into Second or Third conditional forms as indicated.

  1. I don't have a car, so I can't drive to work. (Second conditional)
  2. He didn't study, so he failed the exam. (Third conditional)
  3. I am not rich, so I don't buy a house. (Second conditional)
  4. She didn't take the umbrella, so she got wet. (Third conditional)
  5. We don't know her number, so we can't call her. (Second conditional)

questions.texte: Rewrite each sentence using the indicated conditional.
questions.reponse: 1. If I had a car, I would drive to work. 2. If he had studied, he wouldn't have failed the exam. 3. If I were rich, I would buy a house. 4. If she had taken the umbrella, she wouldn't have got wet. 5. If we knew her number, we would call her.

sousQuestions.texte: When do we use 'were' instead of 'was' in the Second conditional?
sousQuestions.reponse: In the Second conditional, we use 'were' for all subjects (I, he, she, it) in formal or standard English.

enonce.texte:
Complete the sentences using Mixed Conditionals (combining Second and Third conditional structures).

  1. If I _______ (be) more careful, I wouldn't have made that mistake.
  2. If she _______ (study) medicine, she would be a doctor now.
  3. If they _______ (not miss) the train, they would be here now.
  4. If I _______ (know) his address, I would have visited him.
  5. If he _______ (speak) French, he would have gotten the job.

questions.texte: Complete the sentences with the correct verb forms.
questions.reponse: 1. were, 2. had studied, 3. hadn't missed, 4. knew, 5. spoke

sousQuestions.texte: Explain the structure of a mixed conditional (past condition - present result).
sousQuestions.reponse: If + past perfect (past condition), would + infinitive (present result).

enonce.texte:
Rewrite the following sentences using I wish or If only to express regret.

  1. I didn't study for the test.
  2. I don't have a better job.
  3. She didn't call me yesterday.
  4. I can't speak English fluently.
  5. He forgot my birthday.

questions.texte: Rewrite each sentence using 'I wish' or 'If only'.
questions.reponse: 1. I wish I had studied for the test. / If only I had studied for the test. 2. I wish I had a better job. / If only I had a better job. 3. I wish she had called me yesterday. / If only she had called me yesterday. 4. I wish I could speak English fluently. / If only I could speak English fluently. 5. I wish he hadn't forgotten my birthday. / If only he hadn't forgotten my birthday.

sousQuestions.texte: What is the difference between 'I wish' for present vs past regrets?
sousQuestions.reponse: For present regrets, use 'I wish' + past simple (I wish I had a car). For past regrets, use 'I wish' + past perfect (I wish I had studied).

enonce.texte:
Read the situations and write an appropriate conditional sentence.

  1. You want to go to the party, but you don't have a ride.
  2. You didn't set your alarm, so you overslept.
  3. You want to buy a new phone, but you don't have enough money.
  4. You missed the bus, and you were late for work.
  5. You are tired because you worked all day.

questions.texte: Write a conditional sentence for each situation.
questions.reponse: 1. If I had a ride, I would go to the party. 2. If I had set my alarm, I wouldn't have overslept. 3. If I had enough money, I would buy a new phone. 4. If I hadn't missed the bus, I wouldn't have been late for work. 5. If I didn't work all day, I wouldn't be tired.

enonce.texte:
You are a manager at a company. Write conditional sentences for the following business scenarios.

  1. The team is not working efficiently because they lack training.
  2. The project was delayed because the supplier was late.
  3. You want to propose a new strategy to increase sales.
  4. A client is unhappy because you didn't deliver on time.
  5. The company is losing money because of poor marketing.

questions.texte: Write a conditional sentence for each business scenario.
questions.reponse: 1. If the team had proper training, they would work more efficiently. 2. If the supplier hadn't been late, the project wouldn't have been delayed. 3. If we implemented a new strategy, we would increase sales. 4. If we had delivered on time, the client wouldn't be unhappy. 5. If we improved our marketing, we wouldn't be losing money.

enonce.texte:
Complete the following sentences with the correct conditional form.

  1. If I _______ (know) the answer, I would tell you.
  2. If she _______ (arrive) early, she would have seen the opening ceremony.
  3. If you heat ice, it _______ (melt).
  4. If they _______ (not leave) now, they will miss the flight.
  5. If he had listened to me, he _______ (not make) that mistake.
  6. If I were you, I _______ (apply) for that job.
  7. If she _______ (be) more careful, she wouldn't have broken the vase.
  8. If we _______ (not take) that route, we would have arrived earlier.

questions.texte: Fill in the blanks with the correct verb forms.
questions.reponse: 1. knew, 2. had arrived, 3. melts, 4. don't leave, 5. wouldn't have made, 6. would apply, 7. had been, 8. hadn't taken

enonce.texte:
Write a short essay (150-200 words) on the following topic:

"If you could change one thing about your country, what would it be and why?"

Use at least five different conditionals (Zero, First, Second, Third, and Mixed) in your essay.

questions.texte: Write an essay using various conditional forms.
questions.reponse: Example: 'If I could change one thing about Cameroon, it would be the education system. First, if students had better resources (Second conditional), they would learn more effectively. If we invest more in education (First conditional), we will see improvements. If the government had prioritized education earlier (Third conditional), we wouldn't have many of today's problems. However, if we work together now (Zero conditional), we can create a better future. I believe that if we had started reforms ten years ago (Third conditional), we would be in a much better position today (Mixed conditional).'

enonce.texte:
Find and correct the errors in these conditional sentences.

  1. If I will see him, I tell him the news.
  2. If she would have studied, she would pass.
  3. If I was you, I would accept the offer.
  4. If he had came earlier, he would have seen her.
  5. If you heat water, it will boil.
  6. If they had not missed the bus, they would be here now.

questions.texte: Find and correct the mistakes in each sentence.
questions.reponse: 1. If I see him, I will tell him the news. 2. If she had studied, she would have passed. 3. If I were you, I would accept the offer. 4. If he had come earlier, he would have seen her. 5. If you heat water, it boils. (Zero conditional) 6. Correct as is.
